title: Cracking the Code: ECEC Teachers’ Pedagogical Practices for Fostering Children’s Mathematical Knowledge and Computational Thinking with Coding Toys
text_snippet: Cracking the Code: ECEC Teachers’ Pedagogical Practices for Fostering Children’s Mathematical Knowledge and Computational Thinking with Coding Toys Coding in early childhood education provides diverse opportunities for developing children’s mathematical knowledge and computational thinking skills. Drawing on more than two years of pedagogical experience integrating coding toys into children’s play activities, this study explores how four early childhood teachers describe their practices for fostering children’s mathematical knowledge and computational thinking. A qualitative case study design was employed, incorporating in-depth individual interviews with video-stimulated recall sessions, and the data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. The findings show that the teachers emphasized the importance of embodied exploration, dialogic interaction, and opportunities for experimentation and problem solving when supporting children’s engagement with coding toys. Rather than relying on the technology itself, the teachers highlighted how their pedagogical mediation helped children connect coding activities with mathematical reasoning and computational thinking. title: Exploring the impact of hybrid and on-ground clinical experiences on early childhood teacher candidate learning outcomes
text_snippet: Exploring the impact of hybrid and on-ground clinical experiences on early childhood teacher candidate learning outcomes Clinical experiences in teacher preparation programs link theory to practice and support teacher candidates’ self-efficacy and preparedness for the field. While research has examined these experiences for developing teaching competencies, few studies have compared the impact of hybrid experiences during the COVID-19 pandemic to on-ground experiences, especially in early childhood education programs that prepare candidates for dual certification in general and special education. This qualitative study explored the differences in candidate learning outcomes – defined here as self-efficacy and preparedness for teaching –between hybrid and fully on-ground clinical experience modalities during the COVID-19 pandemic among early childhood teacher candidates seeking dual certification. We conducted focus group interviews with six recent graduates, who engaged in either a hybrid or an on-ground experience. Thematic analysis of the interview data yielded themes centered on self-efficacy and preparedness that explained our candidates’ competencies. title: Dimensions of Embodied Learning: An Observation of Children’s Embodied Expressions in ECE Settings in Finland
text_snippet: Dimensions of Embodied Learning: An Observation of Children’s Embodied Expressions in ECE Settings in Finland Every child has the right to express themselves and be understood based on their unique abilities. Supporting children’s own ways of communicating, including recognizing embodied expressions, is essential for learning. This study investigates dimensions of embodied learning observable in Finnish early childhood education (ECE) settings, focusing on how children’s embodied expressions and interactions contribute to meaning-making and learning. Drawing on the theory of embodied cognition, the study analyzes how non-verbal communication – including bodily, emotional, and social expressions – enables children’s active meaning-making and learning. The data consists of video recordings of twelve children (aged 3–5) during three learning activities. The material was analysed using a coding framework for embodied cognition and thematic content analysis to identify recurring patterns of embodied learning. The results demonstrate that embodied expressions, where bodily, emotional, and social experiences are inherent to cognitive processes, play a vital role in children’s learning. title: Craft Education within Early Childhood Education – A Potential Resource or a Practical Challenge? Slöjdfostran inom småbarnspedagogik - Potentiell resurs eller praktisk utmaning?
text_snippet: Craft Education within Early Childhood Education – A Potential Resource or a Practical Challenge? Slöjdfostran inom småbarnspedagogik - Potentiell resurs eller praktisk utmaning? Craft in early childhood education (ECE) plays an important role in promoting children’s creative and practical skills, yet it remains underrepresented. The aim of this study is to highlight the conditions that staff perceive they have when implementing craft activities in ECE contexts. The study is part of a R&D project conducted at Åbo Akademi University 2023–2025 and is based on a digital survey completed by 54 individuals in Swedish-speaking ECE in Finland in autumn 2023. The survey included closed and open-ended questions concerning staff experiences, institutional conditions, and the design of craft activities. The findings show that craft activities are shaped by an interplay between children’s developmental levels, staff members’ subject-related confidence, access to materials and tools, the physical environment, group dynamics, and organizational and time-related conditions. Safety emerges as a cross-cutting concern influencing all stages of the process. Limited access to appropriate spaces, insufficient resources, and varying competence challenge opportunities for in-depth and creative craft activities. title: Inklusiivista leikkiä ja aikuisen emotionaalista saatavillaoloa kannatteleva leikkipedagogiikka Play pedagogy promoting inclusive play and adult emotional availability
text_snippet: Inklusiivista leikkiä ja aikuisen emotionaalista saatavillaoloa kannatteleva leikkipedagogiikka Play pedagogy promoting inclusive play and adult emotional availability Play has been studied for several decades. However, in the context of early childhood education and care (ECEC) and pre-primary education, it remains true that not all children are able to participate in joint play, which can pose a risk to their development and well-being. The aim of this study is to explore which kinds of play environments, practices, and structures support the participation of all children and sustain the adults´ emotional availability during free play situations indoors. The data were collected during the 2022–2023 school year from three groups in a medium-sized Finnish city that participated in the Finnish two-year pre-primary education trial in 2021–2023. The data consists of three semi-structured theme interviews conducted with teams and the groups’ documented early childhood education plans. The data were analysed using Braun and Clarke’s six-phase reflexive thematic analysis. Four main themes were identified: (1) Play under the pressure of time, resources, and other activities, (2) Aiming for calm, uninterrupted play, (3) Methods and practices guiding adults´ actions, and (4) Adults’ prior experiences and beliefs about their own play competence. title: Participation during educational transitions of children with special educational needs – Early childhood education professionals’ perspectives
text_snippet: Participation during educational transitions of children with special educational needs – Early childhood education professionals’ perspectives Children’s participation during educational transitions reveals the opportunities and constraints embedded in early childhood education and care practices, but its implementation remains uneven. This study explores how early childhood education professionals (ECEP) perceive and describe the participation of children with special educational needs (SEN) during educational transitions, focusing on the opportunities and constraints that shape children’s participation. Survey responses from Swedish-speaking ECEPs (N = 60) were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis informed by critical realism. The results showed that participation was not guaranteed; it was constrained by structural priorities and adult-led routines conditioned by age and communication skills, but also supported through pedagogy and adult scaffolding. We identified tensions between ideals and practice alongside opportunities to strengthen participation. The findings highlight three key strategies: responsive pedagogy, multimodal communication and structured coordination. title: Effects of Representational Gestures on Preschool Children’s Story Comprehension and Word Learning
text_snippet: Effects of Representational Gestures on Preschool Children’s Story Comprehension and Word Learning Gestures are in integral part of human communication and observing gestures during storytelling might increase recipients’ learning and memory because they add visual information to speech. In the present study, we examined the effects of representational gestures on preschool children’s story comprehension and word learning from a story. To do so, 89 three- to six-year-old German preschool children listened to a videotaped story either without gestures or with representational gestures. After the story presentation, story comprehension and receptive and expressive target-word tests were administered. Listening to a videotaped storytelling with gestures increased children’s receptive and expressive target-word learning as well as their story comprehension significantly compared to the version without gestures. The effects did not depend on children’s age. Including representational gestures during storytelling is a promising way for helping children to get a better grasp of spoken information and to acquire new words. title: Implementing co-teaching in pre-primary education – a Finnish multiple case study
text_snippet: Implementing co-teaching in pre-primary education – a Finnish multiple case study This study examined co-teaching between early childhood special education teachers (ECSETs) and early childhood education teachers (ECTs) in two Finnish pre-primary education groups, aiming to understand how ECSETs and ECTs can implement co-teaching as a teaching approach that benefits children’s learning and participation as well as teachers’ professionalism in pre-primary education. A multiple case study design was used. The study included two different cases comprising two co-teaching pairs (ECSET and ECT), who co-taught in two different pre-primary education groups. The results showed differences and similarities between the cases. Both co-teaching pairs chose one co-teaching approach to which they adhered. One pair decided to split the group and teach the children in different rooms, while the other pair chose to teach all the children together in the same room. Both co-teaching pairs also found that it became easier to meet the children’s individual needs in a common group. The pair which taught all children together also experienced that co-teaching benefited the teachers’ professional development, which was not evident in the experiences of the pair that divided the group.

title: Move over, Alfie Atkins! On representation in read-aloud literature in early childhood education Maka på dig, Alfons Åberg! Om representation i småbarnspedagogikens bokstundsböcker

Om representation i småbarnspedagogikens bokstundsböcker This study examines reading sessions and book selection practices within Swedish‑medium early childhood education in Finland, with a particular focus on their potential to foster recognition and broaden children’s perspectives. The study explores the range of books children encounter, how gender and skin tones are represented, and how staff perceive the significance of representation. The study includes 148 participants and is based on a web survey addressing the books used and the purposes of reading sessions. The qualitative content analysis shows that the books vary in age but are exclusively of Western origin, with books published in Sweden constituting the clear majority. The selection is dominated by white and male protagonists, while dark‑skinned protagonists occur rarely. In the participants’ reflections on book selection and reading sessions, awareness of diversity appears limited, although many highlight reading sessions as important opportunities for social learning and a sense of community. title: Jännitteet, siirtymät ja yhteistyö esi- ja alkuopetuksen opettajien vertaisryhmäkeskusteluissa Tensions, transition and collaboration in pre-primary and primary teacher peer group discussions
text_snippet: Jännitteet, siirtymät ja yhteistyö esi- ja alkuopetuksen opettajien vertaisryhmäkeskusteluissa Tensions, transition and collaboration in pre-primary and primary teacher peer group discussions The starting point for this study was to develop, together with the teachers, a transition cooperation in pre-primary and primary education in a northern Finnish municipality. The research question was what kind of tensions can be identified in the transitions between pre-primary and primary education, and how transition practices are developed and common understanding is built around tensions. The material for the study consisted of peer group discussions (n = 4 times) conducted by teachers during the academic year 2023–2024. In the analysis of the data, a situational mapping method based on anchored theory was applied. The theoretical starting point of the study is the idea that people live their daily life in certain operating environments, which are influenced by relationships between different environments and broader contexts. The results of the study identified tensions in relation to children, parents, the work community, and guiding documents. title: The Complexity of Intersubjectivity in ECEC: Using Drawing as a Method of Inquiry
text_snippet: The Complexity of Intersubjectivity in ECEC: Using Drawing as a Method of Inquiry This study explores intersubjectivity in early childhood education and care (ECEC) through interaction and drawing analyses. It highlights the interactions between a teacher and two children, emphasising the mechanisms that either hinder or promote intersubjectivity. Using micro-level ethnographic methods, data from video observations are analysed with theoretical concepts from the theory of play-responsive teaching. The aim is to contribute to understanding the complexities of intersubjectivity and to show how drawing analysis, in combination with interaction analysis, may enhance insight into the complexities. The integration of drawing and interaction analyses reveals that different interpretations of objects by children and educators significantly influence the formation of intersubjectivity. This finding encourages a discussion on potential shifts in the concept of intersubjectivity, expanding it beyond merely interpersonal aspects within the theory of play-responsive teaching. Broadening the scope of intersubjectivity can also impact pedagogical practices, such as in the establishment of joint activities.

title: Reflektion merkitys relationaalisen asiantuntijuuden rakentumisessa varhaiskasvatuksen tiimeissä The role of reflection in the development of relational expertise in early childhood education and care teams
text_snippet: Reflektion merkitys relationaalisen asiantuntijuuden rakentumisessa varhaiskasvatuksen tiimeissä The role of reflection in the development of relational expertise in early childhood education and care teams This study examined the construction of relational expertise in multi-professional teams in early childhood education and care (ECEC). The aim of the study was to identify how the aspects of relational expertise are related to each other. The study utilized survey data from VUOKKO -research for ECEC professionals (n = 203). The variables were theoretically constructed, and their relationships were analyzed using hierarchical regression analysis. The results showed that joint reflection was the single most important aspect of building relational expertise. The focus of multi-professional teams in ECEC should therefore be on reflective discussions to bring out everyone's expertise and thus build common knowledge and expertise. The implementation of reflection skills already during the training phase can facilitate the realization of multiprofessional collaboration by utilizing each professional´s expertise.

title: Vuorovaikutus varhaiskasvatuksen ruokailutilanteissa: Havainnointitutkimus kasvatushenkilöstön sosiaalisista orientaatioista Interaction During Mealtimes in Early Childhood Education and Care: An Observational Study of Educators' Social Orientations

However, the pedagogy of mealtimes and educator–child interaction in these contexts has been discussed only to a limited extent in Finnish research. This article responds to this need for up-to-date knowledge by investigating what kinds of social orientations occur among educators during ECEC mealtimes in relation to the age of the child group and other ECEC activities. In addition, we examine how educators’ orientations are linked to children's emotions and involvement. The data consists of child observations (N = 341,091), which were collected as part of the Progressive Feedback project between 2017 and 2024. Cross-tabulation and chi-square tests were used in the quantitative analysis. The results showed that neutral, routine-focused orientation was emphasised during mealtimes when compared to other ECEC activities. title: Check in Check out -tukimalli varhaiskasvatuksessa The Check In Check Out Intervention in Early Childhood Education and Care
text_snippet: Check in Check out -tukimalli varhaiskasvatuksessa The Check In Check Out Intervention in Early Childhood Education and Care In early childhood education and care, it is important to provide both group-based and individually tailored early and needs-based support to promote children's well-being and social development. Recent research emphasizes that supporting socio-emotional and behavioral skills is most effective when implemented systematically and through evidence-based methods. One such support model is Check in Check out (CICO), which has been shown to be effective in promoting appropriate behavior in school settings. However, research on its applicability in early childhood education and care remains limited. This study examined the effectiveness and acceptability of the CICO intervention in Finnish early childhood education units implementing Positive Behavior Interventions and Supports (PBIS) framework (named ProVaka). The study was conducted using a single-case experimental design. Behavioral changes in three children were followed during the CICO intervention based on evaluations provided by early childhood education and care staff. title: Possibilities of Eye-tracking on Reflecting Teachers' Expertise in Early Childhood Education and Care
text_snippet: Possibilities of Eye-tracking on Reflecting Teachers' Expertise in Early Childhood Education and Care Teachers' visual gaze plays an important role in practicing pedagogy and interaction in early childhood education and care (ECEC). Combining the exploration of visual gaze with a think-aloud method enables the study of teachers’ reflections on the cognitive processes behind their gaze. Video observation has been stated to be an effective way for teachers to reflect on and learn from their actions. The aim of our study was to explore ECEC teachers’ reflections as they watched eye-tracking recordings of themselves and through interviews that aimed to evaluate and develop their expertise. The participants were six ECEC teachers of groups of under three-year-old children, who had participated in the data collection implemented with eye-tracking glasses during pedagogical activities. The data consisted of 12 semi-structured interviews (two per teacher). Interviews were accompanied with the visual observation of teachers’ own eye-tracking videos and retrospective think-aloud methods. The study applied discourse analysis. title: Encounters with social class in class-evasive ECEC: Staff's and children's experiences
text_snippet: Encounters with social class in class-evasive ECEC: Staff's and children's experiences In this article, we examine if and how social class influences children's interactions and experiences in the Early Childhood Education and Care (ECEC) setting. By examining these dynamics and using Bourdieu´s theory of capital and habitus, we can better understand the impact of social class on children's development and the critical role ECEC plays in reproducing or reducing social inequalities. The data include observations from 18 ECEC centres and interviews with 74 staff members in Swedish-speaking ECEC in Finland. The observations included informal discussions with the children during organised activities and free play for one month at each ECEC centre. The data were analysed with critical discourse analysis. The results show that staff on most occasions take a class-evasive approach. They reject discussions about social class and avoid the terminology. Instead, they often talk about differences between families in terms of different attitudes and time resources. However, observations reveal how children experiencing economic disadvantage carefully navigate interactions around birthdays and holiday celebrations due to a lack of economic resources. title: Lapsen esteettisen toimijuuden ilmentymiä varhaiskasvatuksen arjessa Children’s aesthetic agency as manifested in everyday early childhood education contexts
text_snippet: Lapsen esteettisen toimijuuden ilmentymiä varhaiskasvatuksen arjessa Children’s aesthetic agency as manifested in everyday early childhood education contexts This article examines child´s aesthetic agency in various situations in the everyday life of institutional early childhood education. The study is grounded in a naturalistic view of the human being as inherently aesthetic, and aesthetic agency is analyzed both through Dissanayake’s (1995, 2013, 2015) five aesthetic primitives and from the perspective of the elements of childhood aesthetics (von Bonsdorff, 2018). The findings show that the children´s aesthetic agency emerges in everyday life whenever even a small opportunity arises. It is also strongly narrative in nature: children’s actions are storytelling practices that unfold as embodied, linguistic, and interactional expression (von Bonsdorff, 2018, p. 126–138). Aesthetic agency is realized intersubjectively – as reaching out to others – as children respond to one another’s gestures, movements, and sounds, continuing and reshaping the expressions initiated by others. This creates a dynamic and ever-evolving space of shared aesthetic agency, a socio-aesthetic agency (Rissanen, 2025, pp. 74–76), in which individual experience and shared aesthetic attunement become intertwined. title: Diskursiiviset jatkuvan oppimisen vastuut varhaiskasvatuksen opettajien puheessa Discursive responsibilities for continuous learning in early childhood education teachers’ talk
text_snippet: Diskursiiviset jatkuvan oppimisen vastuut varhaiskasvatuksen opettajien puheessa Discursive responsibilities for continuous learning in early childhood education teachers’ talk Early childhood education teachers´ continuous learning enhances the quality of early childhood education and care (ECEC) and supports children's growth, learning, and well-being. This study examines the responsibility discourses related to ECEC teachers’ continuous learning. The research data consists of thematic interviews with 13 ECEC teachers and was analyzed using discourse analysis. The findings identify four distinct responsibility discourses: (1) responsibility for personal learning, (2) responsibility assigned to the leader, (3) burdensome responsibility, and (4) responsibility of the teacher-leader. The results indicate that teachers perceive taking responsibility for their own continuous learning as a legitimate practice, although the enactment of this responsibility appears fragmented. The role of the leader as a facilitator of learning is highly significant, yet the expectations placed on leaders may be unrealistic. Teachers also describe the responsibility for learning as burdensome. journal_name: Journal of Early Childhood Education Research
title: Work engagement of novice ECEC teachers: psychological safety in terms of personal and workplace resources
text_snippet: Work engagement of novice ECEC teachers: psychological safety in terms of personal and workplace resources This study examined novice early childhood education (ECEC) teachers’ work engagement in the early induction phase of their career through interview analysis. Three types of work engagement narratives were identified: decreasing, hesitant and strong. Furthermore, the study examined how psychological safety is described in different kinds of ECEC teachers’ work engagement narratives in terms of workplace and personal resources. The study illustrates that both personal and workplace resources are needed to promote psychological safety and work engagement. Novice ECEC teachers’ ability to balance work and personal life, not being left alone, trust, self-efficacy, and not having their professional ability questioned in the work community were identified as key resources in promoting psychological safety and work engagement.

title: “What's your hurry?” – Tensions of time in pedagogical leadership
text_snippet: “What's your hurry?” – Tensions of time in pedagogical leadership Early childhood centre leaders (leaders) state that they do not have enough time for pedagogical leadership (FINEEC, 2023; OAJ, 2020; Siippainen et al., 2021). In this study, pedagogical leadership is understood broadly, encompassing most of a leader's tasks aiming to lead, influence, or develop pedagogy (see Heikka et al., 2024; Kristiansen et al., 2021; Parrila & Fonsén, 2017). The aim of the study is to analyse the ways in which leaders reflect on time in relation to pedagogical leadership. The theoretical framing is based on an analytical perspective on time in ECEC intertwined with social constructionism (Burr, 2015). The data collection was carried out in 2022-2023 through semi-structured interviews with leaders (N = 14) from Swedish-speaking parts of Finland. A qualitative analysis was conducted using discourse analysis as methodological approach (Anderson & Holloway, 2020; Haider & Bawden, 2007). The analysis yielded four discourses, which articulate that time in relation to pedagogical leadership is characterised by dealing with strict clock time, demands and lack of time, but it also invites reflective presence in the moment. title: “Again, It Depends on Numbers and People Coming”: Institution-initiated Transitions in Early Childhood Education and Care
text_snippet: “Again, It Depends on Numbers and People Coming”: Institution-initiated Transitions in Early Childhood Education and Care This study examines the constitution of institution-initiated transitions emerging during children’s years in early childhood education and care (ECEC) with a relational approach. The aim is to trace connections between the socio-political context and transitions. The socio-political context is seen as a transition system producing varying transition patterns. Longitudinal interview data with educators about five focus children’s transitions in Finnish ECEC was analysed. The study uses the premises of Walther’s (2006) transition regime model as a heuristic analysis tool. Patterns of relationality (Settersten et al., 2022) are employed to describe mechanisms that constitute transitions. The main findings are that, firstly, children’s transitions are constituted by the interaction between the structural ECEC pathway and local micro-regimes emerging in relation to local freedom to organise ECEC services. Secondly, the rationales for transitions are often managerial. title: Yliopistollisen harjoittelupäiväkodin opettajat uuden toimintajärjestelmän äärellä Teachers’ new activity system in a university-owned ECEC centre
text_snippet: Yliopistollisen harjoittelupäiväkodin opettajat uuden toimintajärjestelmän äärellä Teachers’ new activity system in a university-owned ECEC centre This article examines the development of the work of early childhood education and early childhood special education teachers in Finland's first university-owned early childhood education and care (ECEC) centre during the first year of its operation. The analysis focuses on teachers’ activity system and on identifying its inner contradictions and the suggestions for formed solutions. The theoretical background of the study is applied from the cultural-historical activity theory and Engeström's (1995) methodology of developmental work research. The data were collected in 2021, during the Covid-19 pandemic, when Early Childhood and Teacher Education Centre (ECTEC) Rauman pikkunorssi started its operations at the Rauma campus of the University of Turku. Data, i.e. remotely organised meetings (N=7) and diaries (N=10) of teachers as well as meeting memos (N=7) of the Pikkunorssi Team, were analysed abductively. As a result, the teacher’s activity system in ECTEC Rauman pikkunorssi is presented. Additionally, contradictions in teachers' activity system and suggestions for their resolution, especially from the point of view of academic collaboration, are presented.

title: How young students’ creation of analog and digital representations, in combination, may contribute to their learning of combinatorics
text_snippet: How young students’ creation of analog and digital representations, in combination, may contribute to their learning of combinatorics In this study, we elaborate on whether – and if so, how – students’ creation of analog and digital representations, in combination, may strengthen their meaning making in combinatorics while engaging in problem solving. An intervention was conducted in two Swedish preschool classes (six-year-olds) involving 25 students. The results indicate that creating a digital animation did not primarily enhance problem solving but rather served as an aid for students to redesign their analog knowledge representations, enabling them to further engage with the mathematical content. A conclusion is that the creation of analog and digital representations, in combination, contributed to students’ explorations of combinatorics and that, when integrated into a learning-design sequence, digital animations enhanced students' understanding of combinatorics. This conclusion should be seen in relation to the small scale of the study, which means that more studies are needed in order to generalize the findings.

title: Preschool teachers’ reflections of their leadership – personal, professional and positional perspectives
text_snippet: Preschool teachers’ reflections of their leadership – personal, professional and positional perspectives The purpose of this study is to investigate preschool teachers' insights into their leadership role, drawing on individual and collective reflections generated during dialogue seminars. Given the complexity of the preschool teacher's leadership, which is shaped by interactions with others and varies across contexts, the study emphasises the personal, professional and positional perspectives of leadership (Saarukka, 2015, 2017; Sergiovanni, 2001). Dialogue seminars (Hammarén, 1999) were used to elicit preschool teachers’ reflections on leadership, and research interviews (Kvale & Brinkman, 2014) were conducted to further explore these insights. The findings show that the participating preschool teachers developed greater self-awareness and a deeper understanding of their leadership identities. They also came to view their leadership in relation to children, guardians and colleagues, highlighting the personal, professional and positional perspectives of the complex leadership role in preschool education. title: Kotipesä – varhaiskasvatuksen fyysinen ja sosiaalinen toimintaympäristö Homebase - the physical and social environment of early childhood education
text_snippet: Kotipesä – varhaiskasvatuksen fyysinen ja sosiaalinen toimintaympäristö Homebase - the physical and social environment of early childhood education Homebases (kotipesä) are a rather new way of organizing early childhood education and are common especially in new early childhood education centers where flexibility of spaces has been considered. Different types of pedagogical solutions and organizational culture are related to the ways of arranging child groups in homebases. This article examines homebase as a flexible form of early childhood education pedagogy. The aim of this study is to examine what kind of physical and social environments homebases are in early childhood education, and how early childhood education teachers experience homebases as a pedagogical environment. The physical environment reflects strongly the way of implementing the pedagogical solutions, and the pedagogy in the homebase. Theoretically, the examination of the homebase is based on a relational concept of space in which the space is understood as constantly changing and structured through everyday practices. The article is based on a master’s thesis. The material was collected by open-ended theme inquiry from early childhood education teachers at the turn of the year 2020. The essays that form the data were analyzed with qualitative content analysis

title: Swedish preschool teachers’ views on and use of digital technology in preschool education
text_snippet: Swedish preschool teachers’ views on and use of digital technology in preschool education Research on digital technology in early childhood education is limited, especially in relation to pedagogical practices and educators’ perspectives. This study investigates views and experiences of digital technology among Swedish preschool teachers focusing on the following two research questions: 1) What are the preschool teachers' views of digital technology in preschool? 2) How do the preschool teachers use digital technology in preschool? A total of 44 interviews were analysed thematically (RQ1) and using a framework of replacement, amplification and transformation (RQ2). The results show that most of the preschool teachers expressed positive views on the use of digital technology in preschool, but also a need for more knowledge about how to use different digital tools. When the preschool teachers talked about teaching and learning, they mentioned the importance of children being producers who actively create digital content, rather than consumers of ready-made digital software. Further, the teachers often expressed that their view depended on how and with whom digital technology was to be used. journal_name: Journal of Early Childhood Education Research
title: Proportionate Universalism as an Approach to Support Physical Activity of Young Children with Disabilities in Childcare Settings
text_snippet: Proportionate Universalism as an Approach to Support Physical Activity of Young Children with Disabilities in Childcare Settings Physical activity is important for young children’s (aged 0-5 years) health and development. However, young children with disabilities have markedly low levels of daily physical activity. While the childcare setting offers a unique environment to target physical activity promotion among young children, several inequalities exist that affect physical activity opportunities for young children with disabilities in these settings. As such, this article discusses the inequality in access to physical activity opportunities for young children with disabilities in childcare settings. It draws on, and suggests that, application of a proportionate universalism approach to promote inclusive physical activity opportunities for young children with disabilities in childcare settings may support participation.

title: Gender and gender equality in research on preschools and ECEC in Sweden 2002-2022
text_snippet: Gender and gender equality in research on preschools and ECEC in Sweden 2002-2022 This article aims to present a research review done of research on gender and gender equality in relation to Swedish Early Childhood Education and Care (ECEC) during 2002–2022. The article is based on a report compiled at the request of the Swedish Gender Equality Authority in fall 2023 and this article highlights the results. Since Sweden historically has been seen as having a prominent position concerning gender equality work the result can be interesting to a larger field of researchers. The studies included were selected through various search methods to find Swedish and/or international research relevant to Swedish preschool conditions. This article puts its focus on studies that are interpreted as being specifically relevant to preschool practice, in terms of how research results could support development and change into a more gender equal preschool in accordance with the Swedish national curricula for preschools, close to the Finnish assignments. title: Koira, jonka nimi on Kissa ja vaari, joka onkin mummo. Lastenkirjallisuuden queer-luenta sukupuolen moninaisuuden edistäjänä A dog called Cat and a grandpa who is actually a grandma. Queer reading in children's literature as a promoter of gender diversity
text_snippet: Koira, jonka nimi on Kissa ja vaari, joka onkin mummo. Lastenkirjallisuuden queer-luenta sukupuolen moninaisuuden edistäjänä A dog called Cat and a grandpa who is actually a grandma. Queer reading in children's literature as a promoter of gender diversity In this article, queer is framed as a concept, as an interest in knowledge, i.e. as a commitment to emancipation, and as the (emerging) identities of the characters in the books we analyse. We present queer theory through the problematization of the concept of gender and discuss queer pedagogy, which critically examines social orders in education by dismantling them. We present a reading of two picturebooks, Koira nimeltään Kissa (“A Dog Called Cat” by Tomi Kontio & Elina Warsta, 2015) and Ensilumi (“The First Snow” by Mila Teräs & Hannamari Ruohonen, 2022) as an example of how corrective queer literacy (Sedgwick, 2003) can be used to raise awareness of differences by challenging gender as a fixed and normative category. We also argue that queer literacy enables identifying and considering differences as intersectional. We suggest queer literacy as a means of promoting a more equal future, but also highlight the queer utopia, which, following Muñoz (2009), is about giving space and possibility for the future to be different. journal_name: Journal of Early Childhood Education Research
title: Promoting equity and gender equality in ECEC: Reflections from a pilot project
text_snippet: Promoting equity and gender equality in ECEC: Reflections from a pilot project This paper describes a pilot project, Plats för fler! Mini (“Room for More! Mini”), that supported service providers in Early Childhood Education and Care (ECEC) to further gender equality and equity through structured plans and everyday practices. The Finnish education system has been based on values such as equity and equality for decades. However, looking at the everyday praxis of ECEC and previous research, these values remain mostly abstract objectives. In this paper, we present the project and discuss its benefits and areas of improvement. The project consisted of two parts: 1) continuing education in the form of online training sessions and 2) an online material bank. The theoretical framework for both parts was norm-critical pedagogy, which also forms the theoretical framework for this paper. We present how this theoretical framework can be implemented in ECEC and continuing education. This paper discusses promoting gender equality and equity as well as a practical application of equality and non-discrimination plans within ECEC. It offers insights to ECEC personnel, researchers, and continuing education providers.

title: Children’s gender constructions in Brazilian Early Childhood Education and Care
text_snippet: Children’s gender constructions in Brazilian Early Childhood Education and Care The present study examines how gender is constructed by four-year-old children in a Brazilian Early Childhood Education and Care (ECEC) setting. The Brazilian context is marked by the omission of discussions about gender in the National Curriculum for ECEC and the rise of conservative groups in the society. The study seeks to show how children’s relationships with adults, in interplay with ECEC spaces, affect how they construct gender. Gender, as a theoretical concept, informed the interpretation and discussion of our findings. A mosaic approach guided the data collection, which consisted of observations and interviews with children, their teachers, and other adults closed to the children’s context both inside and outside the setting. Data were analysed based on thematic analysis with an inductive approach. The findings reveal how the organisation of pedagogical work and the different roles taken by teachers in the class may influence children’s gender constructions. Children’s relationships with their teachers and other adults also show how stereotypical gender assumptions are both reproduced and challenged during play and other situations in the ECEC setting. title: How do orientations matter in early childhood education? Children, choices and gendering processes
text_snippet: How do orientations matter in early childhood education? Children, choices and gendering processes This paper explores children’s “own” choices in relation to gendering in ECE. Specifically, it problematizes what is often referred to as children’s “own” choices within child-centred pedagogies and emphasises how children’s choices are effects of entangled material-discursive processes, rather than expressions of pre-existing will or intention. To explore this, I re-turn (to) parts of the data and earlier analyses enacted within a research study on science and gender in preschool, together with Sarah Ahmed’s thoughts on orientations. To make re-turnings does not mean to reflecting on, or just going back to a past that was, but re-turning as in turning the data/earlier study over and over again to try to create something new or different. Through these re-turnings, a multifaceted understanding of children’s “own” choices is highlighted, that takes both gender norms, social relations, embodiment, historicity/time, materials and places, learning opportunities, as well as children’s development of capacities and skills into account. title: Uuskonservatismin ja -liberalismin risteyksessä. text_snippet: Uuskonservatismin ja -liberalismin risteyksessä. Hallinnan rationaliteetit varhaiskasvatuksen tasa-arvosuunnitteluvelvoitetta vastustavissa esityksissä At the Intersection of Neoconservatism and Neoliberalism: Rationalities of Government in Discourses Opposing the Gender Equality Planning Obligation in Early Childhood Education Gender equality in Finland has a strong and multi-layered legal foundation. The Finnish education system has aimed to promote equality and gender equality, but methods have varied over time and across different levels of the education system. Policies aimed at promoting equality have been contentious in the field of education, and the concept of equality has meant different things at different times. This study examines the types of problem representations that challenged, resisted, or questioned the obligation to draft gender equality plans in early childhood education, as constructed in the context of the reform of the Equality Act. It also explores the rationalities of governance that these representations reflect. The data consist of stakeholder and expert statements submitted in response to the government proposal to amend the Equality Act. Carol Bacchi's (2009) WPR approach was applied in the analysis. title: Gender Inequality Problems and their (Im)possibilities: Critically Exploring Swedish Preschool’s Gender Equality Mandate
text_snippet: Gender Inequality Problems and their (Im)possibilities: Critically Exploring Swedish Preschool’s Gender Equality Mandate The Swedish preschool has had a gender equality mandate for over two decades. Research shows, however, that preschool teachers find the gender equality mandate challenging to interpret. The aim of this article is to critically explore the theoretical complexities of the gender equality mandate problem constructions and the subsequent (im)possibilities for interpretation. The gender equality mandate encompasses law and curriculum, which are official procedures established and communicated by governmental bodieslocated in five different versions of curricula, the Education Act (SFS, 2010:567), the Discrimination Act (SFS, 2008:567), and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (1989). This constellation is analysed through a Bacchi-inspired critical policy analysis based on diffraction, where gender equality is framed as an essentially contested empty and floating signifier that is filled with different feminist theoretical problem formulations over time and space. title: Done with Gender: Reinforcing and Reproducing Gender Stereotypes and Positions in Early Childhood Education
text_snippet: Done with Gender: Reinforcing and Reproducing Gender Stereotypes and Positions in Early Childhood Education In recent decades, gender issues have received much attention in early childhood education and care (ECEC) in Finland. Gender equality and gender-sensitive education are explicitly mentioned as goals in the national ECEC curriculum. According to the national core curriculum, the staff should be aware of gender issues, actively promote a gender-sensitive environment, and actively strive to treat children equally and equitably. The aim of this study was to investigate how ECEC staff understand and implement gender-sensitive education. It was part of a large multi-sited ethnographic study conducted in ECEC centres. Participatory observations were made of the interactions between staff and children, and among the children, for one month in 18 ECEC centres. In addition, 74 semi-structured interviews were conducted with the ECEC staff. The findings indicate that, despite occasionally questioning the status quo, the staff continued to reinforce and reproduce stereotypical gender divisions, for example by dividing children into girl-pairs and boy-pairs during daily activities. text_snippet: Politics of belonging in the peer relationships of 3–5-year-old children: An ethnographic study of an integrated group in early childhood education and care in Finland Kuulumisen politiikat 3–5-vuotiaiden lasten vertaissuhteissa: Etnografinen tutkimus varhaiskasvatuksen integroidussa lapsiryhmässä Belonging is a key factor in supporting young children’s learning, well-being, and development. Peer relationships in early childhood education and care (ECEC), in particular, are important arenas for young children to construct belonging. However, belonging is often intertwined with questions of power, social positions, hierarchies, and acceptance, notably among young children still practicing interaction. This ethnographic study examined how politics of belonging are manifested in the peer relationships of 3–5-year-old children in an integrated ECEC group setting, where approximately half of the children receive intensified or special support, and the remaining half do not. The group included 12 children (5 of whom received special support) and 5 early childhood professionals. The ethnographic observation data was analyzed using a data-driven thematic analysis. title: A Conceptual Framework for Teaching Addition, Subtraction, and Multiplication in Kindergarten Using Grid-Counting Approach
text_snippet: A Conceptual Framework for Teaching Addition, Subtraction, and Multiplication in Kindergarten Using Grid-Counting Approach This paper presents a conceptual framework for teaching basic arithmetic operations – addition, subtraction, and multiplication – at the kindergarten level using the Hundred Chart. Based on developmental learning theories and supported by a comprehensive literature review, the proposed approach bridges the gap between concrete manipulatives and abstract mathematical reasoning. While not reporting empirical findings, this framework lays the groundwork for future experimental research into developmentally appropriate numeracy strategies in early childhood education. We contend that this visual and structured method, when incorporated in the early grade curriculum, will foster counting fluency, number sense, and operational understanding in a way that is accessible and engaging for young learners. Researchers and teacher educators looking for developmentally appropriate methods, as well as classroom practitioners and curriculum developers hoping to make maths education more tangible and interesting for younger students, can all benefit from this framework.

title: Oppimisentarinan käytettävyys formatiivisen arvioinnin välineenä perusopetuksen alaluokilla The usability of learning stories as a formative assessment tool in lower primary education
text_snippet: Oppimisentarinan käytettävyys formatiivisen arvioinnin välineenä perusopetuksen alaluokilla The usability of learning stories as a formative assessment tool in lower primary education This study investigates the pedagogical usability of a learning story method as part of the formative assessment of 6–9-year-old pupils in the early years education by examining the experiences of class teacher students. Learning stories describe adult’s observations of a child’s learning and offer suggestions for new learning goals and ways to achieve them. The data of the study were collected as part of a guided pre-service training in classroom teacher education in grades 1–3 of primary education. The research data consists of group discussions (N = 9) implemented at the end of the pre-service training, involving 29 pre-service teachers. The data were analyzed in two stages: In the first stage, a theory-driven content analysis was performed with the aim of analyzing students' experiences of the usability of learning story method from the perspective of formative assessment. The unit of this analysis was the expressions in which the students described their experience and its different aspects. title: Varhaiskasvatuksen ja esi- ja alkuopettajien kokemuksia lasten käsityö- ja teknologiaprojektien ohjaamista tukevista tekijöistä
text_snippet: Varhaiskasvatuksen ja esi- ja alkuopettajien kokemuksia lasten käsityö- ja teknologiaprojektien ohjaamista tukevista tekijöistä Tässä tutkimuksessa tarkastellaan, mitkä tekijät tukevat lasten käsityö- ja teknologiaprojektien ohjaamista varhaiskasvatuksessa sekä esi- ja alkuopetuksessa. Tutkimuksessa keskitytään pienten oppilaiden oppimisprosesseja ohjaavien opettajien ja muun henkilökunnan kokemuksiin käsityö- ja teknologiaprojektien ohjaamisesta. Tutkimusaineisto pohjautuu ryhmähaastatteluihin (N = 7) sekä henkilöstön laatimiin käsityö- ja teknologiakasvatuksen kehittämissuunnitelmiin (N = 9). Aineisto analysoitiin laadullisella sisällönanalyysilla. Analyysissa aineistosta muodostui kolme pääteemaa käsityö- ja teknologiaprojektien ohjaamiseen liittyvistä tekijöistä: 1) lasten aktiivinen toiminta, 2) monipuoliset oppimisympäristöt, sekä 3) yhteisopetus ja yhteisöllisyys. Käsityö- ja teknologiakasvatuksen projekteissa keskeisestä oli lasten aktiivisen suunnittelu- ja työskentelytaitojen tukeminen. Yhteisopetus sekä yhteistyö lapsen perheen ja koulun ulkopuolisten tahojen kanssa korostui henkilöstön kokemuksissa. Laajenevat oppimisympäristöt, kuten metsän hyödyntäminen opetuksessa, koettiin tärkeänä oppimisen edistäjänä. journal_name: Journal of Early Childhood Education Research
title: “The decision to leave didn't come overnight” – A discourse analysis of early childhood education teachers’ turnover
text_snippet: “The decision to leave didn't come overnight” – A discourse analysis of early childhood education teachers’ turnover The turnover of early childhood education (ECE) teachers has gained global attention, as the absence of stable and qualified staff challenges the continuity and quality of early childhood education and care. This study examines how former ECE teachers in Finland discursively constructed their turnover decisions. Data were collected through an online survey and analysed using discourse analysis of open-ended responses. The findings show that former ECE teachers accounted for their turnover by constructing a view of Finnish early childhood education, and more broadly Finnish working life, in which unresolved frustration, and ethical strain undermined the sustainability of a calling. When organizational conditions no longer allowed teachers to enact their moral values, turnover was legitimised as a rational and morally grounded decision. These findings highlight how organizational and societal conditions shape the moral viability of retention in early childhood education and provide insights for policymakers, teacher educators, and organizations aiming to reduce avoidable turnover through structural and ethical reforms.

title: Varhaiskasvatuksen opettajaopintoihin hakeutumisen kerronnalliset resurssit Students Narrating their Entry into Early Childhood Teacher Education
text_snippet: Varhaiskasvatuksen opettajaopintoihin hakeutumisen kerronnalliset resurssit Students Narrating their Entry into Early Childhood Teacher Education Efforts to address the workforce shortage in early childhood education (ECEC) and care have primarily focused on increasing student enrolment; however, the appeal of the field appears to be diminishing. Research indicates that the motivation of prospective students is crucial to their commitment to both teacher education programs and the teaching profession itself. This motivation is thought to encompass various influencing factors. In this article, we examine the narratives of ten students about their motivations for applying to early childhood education teacher training, based on interviews. Specifically, we investigate what we coin as ´narrative resources´ students employ to articulate their motivations as integral components of their life stories. The accounts of students reveal that positive experiences working with children serve as crucial life events that substantiate their motivations for entering the ECEC field.
